'''William J. Nellis''' is an American [[physicist]]. He is an associate of the Physics Department of [[Harvard University]].<ref name=HARV>{{cite web|url=https://cambridgeblog.org/author-profile/willaim-j-nellis/|title=William J. Nellis|website=Cambridge University Press|access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> His work has focused on ultra-condensed matter at extreme pressures, densities and temperatures achieved by fast dynamic compression. 

He is the recipient of the [[Bridgman Award]] of AIRAPT,<ref name=brig>{{cite web|url=https://www.airapt.org/?q=node/5|title=Bridgman Award recipients|website=International Association for the Advancement of High Pressure Science and Technology}}</ref> the Duvall Award of APS<ref name=duv>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/shock.cfm|title=George E. Duvall Shock Compression Science Award|website=American Physical Society|access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> and is a fellow of the APS Division of [[condensed matter physics|Condensed Matter Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/william_nellis|title=William Nellis}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Nellis received his B.S. degree in Physics from [[Loyola University Chicago|Loyola University of Chicago]], College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, in 1963 and his Ph.D. degree in Physics from [[Iowa State University]] in 1968.{{cn|date=May 2025}}

== Career and work ==
From 1970 to 1973, Nellis was assistant professor of Physics at [[Monmouth College]] (ILL). In 1973, he left Monmouth to join [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] (LNLL). There he made the first experimental observation of a [[Metallic hydrogen|metallic phase of dense hydrogen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nytimes.com/1996/03/26/science/big-gun-makes-hydrogen-into-a-metal.html|title=Big Gun Makes Hydrogen Into a Metal|website=The New York Times|date=26 March 1996 |access-date=May 19, 2025 |last1=Browne |first1=Malcolm W. }}</ref>

In 2004, Nellis joined the Department of Physics at Harvard University as an associate.{{cn|date=May 2025}}

Nellis was the president of International Association for the Advancement of High Pressure Science and Technology from 2003 to 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.airapt.org/?q=node/7 |title=Past Presidents|website=International Association for the Advancement of High Pressure Science and Technology|access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref>

*2001 - [[Bridgman Award]] of the International Association for the Advancement of High Pressure Science and Technology<ref name=brig/>
